RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

Both you and the successful candidate are men, making it highly improbable that sex discrimination played a role in choosing between you. While an all-male panel at a public broadcaster may reflect outdated panel-composition practices or a procedural flaw under internal diversity policies, it does not substantiate an individual claim of sex bias against you. 

The decision appears tied to skills: the broadcaster specifically cited "strong experience of digital media," suggesting strategic priorities favored digital transformation over your longer, traditional tenure. 

Raising the panel’s gender makeup risks appearing ungrounded and could damage your professional reputation. Instead, politely follow up on your written feedback request, focusing questions strictly on how to bridge the digital experience gap.
